newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 29.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
---------- DAILY NEWS SUB-STANDARD SRI LANKAN FISH EXPORTS IRKS EU

Sri Lanka's fish exports to the European Union could stop if local producers don't improve quality. The EU has warned the Ministry of Fisheries that crustacean fish from Sri Lanka did not meet its quality standards by end of this month. A Ministry spokesman attributed the poor quality to the deterioration of the fishery harbours. The Ministry has requested the EU to grant a grace period up to July 31, 1998.
------ THE ISLAND NO PERMISSION FROM LTTE TO SEE ABDUCTED VILLAGERS

The International Committee of the Red Cross has been unable to see villagers from eastern Irakkakandy and the crew of MV Misen who are being held by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels. Amnesty International recently appealed to LTTE that access be allowed to the prisoners.

The villagers were kidnapped by LTTE earlier this month and ship was attacked and torched off northwestern Mannar around the same time. The rebels released the two Indonesian crew of the ship, but are still holding seve, all Sri Lankans. ------
DINAMINA SIX ARRESTED FOR INCITING STUDENTS

Six people were arrested on Monday by the southern Matara police for trying to incite students of a local school to join a protest campaign against proposed educational reforms. The arrests were made following a complaint by the school principal.
------ DIVAINA ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICERS RESENT POLITICAL PRESSURE

The president of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service Officers' Association, S. Rannuge, has said that officers serving in various parts of the country face political pressure, which prevents them from performing their duties efficiently and without fear. He said officers are transferred if they do not carry out the wishes of the politicians.
------ VIRAKESARI SRI LANKA DENIES MILITARY SHOT AT INDIAN FISHERMEN

Sri Lanka has told India that neither the its navy nor the air force was involved in the recent attacks on Indian fishermen within Indian territorial waters and that there is no evidence to prove that such attacks were ever carried out.
Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar briefed the Indian envoy in Sri Lanka on Monday and refuted all allegations by Indian authorities that such incidents took place on July 14 and 17.
----- THINAKARAN TAMIL PARTIES ASKED TO SUBMIT VIEWS ON ELECTORAL REFORMS

Officials of the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs met representatives of Tamil political parties on Monday to explain the government's draft electoral reforms, and requested them to submit their views on the proposals at a meeting scheduled for Thursday between them and the Minister.
------ THINAKKURUL SHIP DENIED PERMISSION TO TAKE REFUGEES TO JAFFNA

Harbour officials at the eastern port city of Trincomalee have denied permission to a ship to carry refugees and pasengers to the northern Jaffna peninsula. They said the permission was denied due to lack of proper facilities on the ship MV Goodwill Guide.
------ DINAMINA COURT REJECTS OPPOSITION PETITIONS ON POLL RESULTS
A court in Sri Lanka rejected three petitions filed by the main opposition United National Party demanding that fresh elections be held for three local government bodies.
